retail_intro: The crowd's story today is a diagnosis: Facebook's biggest one-day drop ever [[n0811]] invites every smartphone owner to argue whether an iPhone privacy prompt or TikTok did it, and PayPal's slide after its own worst-ever day [[n0733]] shows the mechanism: a record drop starts a change of owners.

retail.title: Meta Platforms / FB — the record crash everyone thinks they understand
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Thursday's session turned an after-hours scare into a record. CNBC reported a 26% plunge, Facebook's biggest one-day drop ever [[n0811]]: Meta Platforms closed at 237.76 USD, down 26.39% on the session and 26.66% below its 324.17 USD close of early January (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). This is the rare crash the crowd feels qualified to diagnose from its own phone, and that familiarity is the hook. If the culprit is a privacy prompt Apple controls, the damage looks like a rule change a giant can work around, and a quarter off the price looks like an overreaction. If it is users drifting to TikTok, the record is only the first chapter.
What Is Driving It

The record arrived with both diagnoses attached. CNBC reported the $232 billion fall set a record for the largest one-day value drop in stock market history [[n1141]]. The Apple diagnosis has the WSJ's $10 billion sting from Apple's privacy push [[n1137]], or Macworld's blunter line that a simple iPhone alert is costing Facebook $10 billion a year [[n1133]]. The competition diagnosis has Business Insider: Facebook's user numbers shrank for the first time in its history [[n1142]], and Zuckerberg says Meta faces unprecedented competition from TikTok [[n1166]]. Reuters reported the wipe-out shook world tech stocks [[n0842]]: the Nasdaq 100 fell 4.22%, Snap lost 23.60% and Pinterest 10.32% before either reported, and the VIX rose 2.26 points to 24.35 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03).
The Social Signal

The attention signal is reach, and the number became the meme, each outlet printing its own record: Bloomberg $251 billion [[n0838]], Business Insider nearly $240 billion [[n1149]], CBS News $237 billion [[n0868]]. Local broadcaster WPTV ran it as a historic drop [[n0843]] and Australia's ABC as a quarter of Meta's value erased [[n1134]]. The retail explainers followed, The Motley Fool on why Meta Platforms stock cratered on Thursday [[n0882]] and Yahoo Finance on the Apple privacy changes that crushed Meta [[n0879]], and so did the scoreboard: Business Insider had Meta below Berkshire Hathaway in market value for the first time in nearly 2 years [[n0841]]. A stock that becomes a number on local television tends to draw buyers who know the app better than the accounts.
Historical Analog

The closest precedent is two days old. PayPal's worst-ever trading day, a 24% drop by CNBC's count [[n0733]], did not mark the low: PYPL fell another 6.24% to 124.30 USD on Thursday, down 21.38% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). The mechanism is a change of owners. A collapse this size turns a growth compounder into a different stock: growth funds must decide whether they want the new story, and value buyers wait for their price. That handover tends to take sessions, not hours, and the size of a fall says nothing about how much of it is done.
Smart Money View

The professionals were not on the sidelines: Bloomberg reported the drop could hit stock funds with $1 trillion that bet on Facebook's parent [[n0837]]. Warren Buffett gave both camps a line, with TheStreet reporting he said he likes Facebook, but not so much its stock [[n0793]]. The bears hold the louder headlines, the New York Times headlining an unmitigated disaster of a quarter [[n0844]] and Forbes an existential moment [[n0808]]. The bulls' best argument is the divide: Reuters framed the miss as a Big Tech split over who's got the data [[n1153]], and CNBC reported Facebook and Google stocks diverged because of Apple [[n0809]]. If the wound is a platform rule that hurts one ad model more than another, it is specific, and it can be engineered around.
When the Narrative Breaks

Three tests matter. First, Thursday's 237.76 USD close (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03): another heavy down day through it would follow PayPal's script. Second, the peers under the same iPhone rule. After the close Reuters reported Pinterest results dazzle Wall St as its ad business booms [[n0856]]; if Friday rewards rivals that grew advertising under Apple's prompt, the Apple alibi weakens and the TikTok diagnosis, the harder one to fix, gains ground. Third, the discount rate. The 2Y Treasury yield has climbed 36 bps over 20 observations to 1.19% in a bear flattening (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-03), and the next jobs number comes with a White House warning that the Omicron spike could skew it [[n2022]]; a surprise either way could reprice the yield that discounts long-dated growth, Meta included.

retail.title: Amazon / AMZN — the giant that answered with AWS
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Amazon is the same evening's comeback story. It fell 7.81% to 2,776.91 USD in Thursday's regular session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), then CNBC reported the shares soaring on a cloud revenue beat and a huge profit gain from the Rivian stake [[n0787]]. Shacknews put AWS revenue up 40% at $17.78 billion [[n0099]], and CNBC reported a $31 billion a year advertising business [[n1128]], sold on its own shopping data, the winning side of what Reuters called the Big Tech divide over who's got the data [[n1153]]. The crowd's read is pricing power, with CNBC reporting Prime going up nearly 17% to $139 a year [[n0784]].
Where It Breaks

The profit has a crack. GeekWire reported Amazon would have posted a $1.8 billion fourth-quarter operating loss without AWS [[n0788]], and the Rivian gain is a mark on an investment, not a sale of goods. Reuters tied the Prime increase to rising wages and costs [[n1129]], an admission that retail is getting dearer to run. The trade breaks if Friday's session cannot hold the after-hours pop: a slide back toward the 2,776.91 USD close would say the market sees a cloud company carrying a struggling retailer.

retail.title: Tesla / TSLA — the record recall you fix by download
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Tesla's faithful have an answer for every scary headline, and it got two tests in a week. Reuters reported a recall of nearly 54,000 vehicles that may disobey stop signs [[n1857]]; then Notebookcheck called the seat-belt recall Tesla's largest ever [[n1917]]. The rebuttal fits in a Teslarati headline: an over-the-air software update will fix the chime on 817k cars [[n1921]]. To believers, a recall that arrives as a download is proof of the moat, and Thursday's tape did not argue: TSLA slipped just 1.60% to 891.14 USD as the Nasdaq 100 fell 4.22%, and is up 7.48% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03). Morgan Stanley, Wccftech reported, sees Tesla's annual revenue exceeding GM's and Ford's combined by 2027 [[n1154]].
Where It Breaks

A download fixes a chime, not the scrutiny. The Washington Post reported Tesla drivers describing a surge in phantom braking [[n1884]], and after two recalls the next complaint is harder to wave away. TSLA is still 18.10% below its 1,088.12 USD close of early January (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03); if it breaks below the 891.14 USD close on the next heavy Nasdaq day, the download defence has stopped protecting the price.

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC — the safe-haven claim gets one good day
parts: Why Retail Is Here

On the day Meta crashed, bitcoin barely blinked: it rose 0.55% to 37,154.60 USD while ether slipped 0.14% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-03), calm that believers tend to read as proof crypto is more than leveraged tech. The Conversation asked why people are calling Bitcoin a religion [[n0966]], and Barron's carried a report calling it better than gold and national currencies [[n1757]]. The crowd's own venues are moving in: Reuters reported investor-focused social media firm Stocktwits rolling out crypto trading [[n1762]]. Even the latest scare was absorbed: after Elliptic sized the Wormhole theft at $325 million [[n0943]], The Defiant reported Jump Crypto replacing over $320M of wrapped ETH [[n0962]].
Where It Breaks

The listed crypto proxies did not share the calm: GBTC fell 3.60%, Coinbase 3.23% and Marathon Digital 7.86% in Thursday's US session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-03), a sign that brokerage-account crypto still trades like tech. Bitcoin sits 13.79% below its 43,099.70 USD close of mid-January (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-03), and a private bailout is no promise the next exploit will be covered. The safe-haven claim breaks the first time bitcoin follows the Nasdaq down on a heavy tech day.
